findings.title: PyYAML: incomplete fix for CVE-2020-1747
PyYAML: arbitrary command execution through python/object/new when FullLoader is used
Image user should not be 'root'
findings.description: Running containers with 'root' user can lead to a container escape situation. It is a best practice to run containers as non-root users, which can be done by adding a 'USER' statement to the Dockerfile.
findings.fix: Add 'USER <non root user name>' line to the Dockerfile

findings.title: missing user
findings.description: Weakness type: CWE-250: Execution with Unnecessary Privileges.
findings.fix: By not specifying a USER, a program in the container may run as 'root'. This is a security hazard. If an attacker can control a process running as root, they may have control over the container. Ensure that the last USER in a Dockerfile is a USER other than 'root'.

findings.title: tainted sql string
findings.description: Weakness type: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes.
findings.fix: Detected user input used to manually construct a SQL string. This is usually bad practice because manual construction could accidentally result in a SQL injection. An attacker could use a SQL injection to steal or modify contents of the database. Instead, use a parameterized query which is available by default in most database engines. Alternatively, consider using the Django object-relational mappers (ORM) instead of raw SQL queries.

findings.title: sqlalchemy execute raw query
findings.description: Weakness type: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection').
findings.fix: Avoiding SQL string concatenation: untrusted input concatenated with raw SQL query can result in SQL Injection. In order to execute raw query safely, prepared statement should be used. SQLAlchemy provides TextualSQL to easily used prepared statement with named parameters. For complex SQL composition, use SQL Expression Language or Schema Definition Language. In most cases, SQLAlchemy ORM will be a better option.

findings.title: subprocess injection
findings.description: Weakness type: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection').
findings.fix: Detected user input entering a `subprocess` call unsafely. This could result in a command injection vulnerability. An attacker could use this vulnerability to execute arbitrary commands on the host, which allows them to download malware, scan sensitive data, or run any command they wish on the server. Do not let users choose the command to run. In general, prefer to use Python API versions of system commands. If you must use subprocess, use a dictionary to allowlist a set of commands.

findings.title: Uncovered a GitHub Personal Access Token, potentially leading to unauthorized repository access and sensitive content exposure.
findings.description: A credential-like value is stored in source code. (The value itself is intentionally left out of this report.)
findings.fix: Revoke and rotate the secret, then load it from an environment variable or a secrets manager instead.

sql injection db cursor execute
findings.description: Weakness type: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection').
findings.fix: User-controlled data from a request is passed to 'execute()'. This could lead to a SQL injection and therefore protected information could be leaked. Instead, use django's QuerySets, which are built with query parameterization and therefore not vulnerable to sql injection. For example, you could use `Entry.objects.filter(date=2006)`.
